newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco expects 3.65 mln T beet, sugar cane output.
newsitem.headline: Morocco expects 3.65 mln T beet, sugar cane output.

text.p: Morocco expects a total sugar crop of 3.65 million tonnes comprising 2.75 million tonnes of beet and 0.9 million tonnes of cane in 1995/96, according to local traders.
A leading local trader told Reuters on Wednesday this was traders' provisional estimate of the crop which had just ended.
The agriculture ministry said official figures may be available next week.

Morocco planted more than 58,353 hectares of beet and 15,129 hectares of sugar cane in 1994/95, which resulted in output of respectively 2.7 million tonnes of beet and 1.04 million tonnes of sugar cane, according to central bank figures.
Traders said they believed the sugar crop area was cut by some 6,000 hectares due to bad weather and floods in 1995/96.
Morocco imported 477,000 tonnes of raw sugar or nearly 50 percent of its total consumption in 1995, the state Office National du The et du Sucre (ONTS) said.
It imported 246,000 tonnes of raw sugar from January to end May 1996, an ONTS official said.
COSUMAR refinery, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, has become Morocco's main sugar importer since sugar liberalisation earlier this year.
"COSUMAR is expected to import up 250,000 tonnes by the end of this year," said a stockbroker in Casablanca, where the firm is located.
The company's officials were not immediately available for comment.
